items.ask: What is the height of Mount Everest above sea level, in metres?

source.title: Mount Everest
source.quote: Its height was most recently measured in 2020 through a joint survey by Nepalese and Chinese authorities as 8,848.86 m (29,031 ft 8+1⁄2 in).

items.ask: In which year was Marie Curie awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics?

source.title: Marie Curie
source.quote: She shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with her husband, Pierre Curie, "for their joint researches on the radioactivity phenomena discovered by Professor Henri Becquerel".

items.ask: Into which ocean does the Amazon River flow?

source.title: Amazon River
source.quote: The Amazon enters Brazil with only one-fifth of the flow it finally discharges into the Atlantic Ocean yet already has a greater flow at this point than the discharge of any other river in the world.

items.ask: Which work by Isaac Newton set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation?

source.title: Isaac Newton
source.quote: His book Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy), first published in 1687, achieved the first great unification in physics and established classical mechanics.

items.ask: Which gas do plants take in from the air during photosynthesis?

source.title: Photosynthesis
source.quote: In this process, atmospheric carbon dioxide is incorporated into already existing organic compounds, such as ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP).

items.ask: Into which sea does the Nile flow?

source.title: Nile
source.quote: The Nile is a major north-flowing river in northeast Africa which empties into the Mediterranean Sea.

items.ask: In which town was Johann Sebastian Bach born?

source.title: Johann Sebastian Bach
source.quote: The Bach family had already produced several composers when Johann Sebastian was born in Eisenach, the youngest child of the city musician Johann Ambrosius Bach.

items.ask: Which 1859 book by Charles Darwin set out the theory of natural selection?

source.title: Charles Darwin
source.quote: Darwin published his theory of evolution with compelling evidence in On the Origin of Species (1859).

items.ask: What is the largest hot desert in the world?

source.title: Sahara
source.quote: The Sahara is the world's largest hot desert.

items.ask: Who created the Python programming language?

source.title: Python (programming language)
source.quote: Guido van Rossum began working on Python in the late 1980s as a successor to the ABC programming language.

items.ask: Who invented the World Wide Web?

source.title: World Wide Web
source.quote: The Web was invented by English computer scientist Tim Berners-Lee while at CERN in 1989 and opened to the public in 1993.

items.ask: Which chemist published the first widely recognised periodic table in 1869?

source.title: Periodic table
source.quote: The first periodic table to become generally accepted was that of the Russian chemist Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869; he formulated the periodic law as a dependence of chemical properties on atomic mass.

items.ask: In which year did the Titanic sink?

source.title: Titanic
source.quote: RMS Titanic was a British ocean liner that sank in the early hours of 15 April 1912 after striking an iceberg on her maiden voyage from Southampton, England, to New York City.

items.ask: In which year did the French Revolution begin?

source.title: French Revolution
source.quote: The French Revolution was a period of political and societal change in France that began with the Estates General of 1789 and ended with the Coup of 18 Brumaire on 9 November 1799.

items.ask: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?

source.title: Berlin Wall
source.quote: The Berlin Wall (German: Berliner Mauer, pronounced [bɛʁˌliːnɐ ˈmaʊɐ] ) was a guarded concrete barrier that encircled West Berlin from 1961 to 1989, separating it from East Berlin and the German Democratic Republic (GDR; East Germany).

items.ask: Who was the first Roman emperor?

source.title: Augustus
source.quote: Augustus (born Gaius Octavius; 23 September 63 BC – 19 August AD 14), also known as Octavian (Latin: Octavianus), was the founder of the Roman Empire and the first Roman emperor from 27 BC until his death in AD 14.

items.ask: How many symphonies did Beethoven compose?

source.title: Ludwig van Beethoven
source.quote: Beethoven's having written nine symphonies was the original source of the so-called curse of the ninth, a superstition that composers were doomed to die before they could complete a tenth symphony.

items.ask: In which town was William Shakespeare born?

source.title: William Shakespeare
source.quote: Shakespeare was born and raised in Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire.

items.ask: On which planet is the Great Red Spot?

source.title: Great Red Spot
source.quote: The Great Red Spot is a persistent, elliptical high-pressure region in the atmosphere of the planet Jupiter, producing the largest anticyclonic storm in the Solar System.

items.ask: What is the deepest known part of Earth's oceans called?

source.title: Mariana Trench
source.quote: The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean, about 200 kilometers (124 mi) east of the Mariana Islands.

items.ask: How many chambers does the human heart have?

source.title: Heart
source.quote: In humans, the heart is divided into four chambers: upper left and right atria and lower left and right ventricles.

items.ask: What does DNA stand for?

source.title: DNA
source.quote: Deoxyribonucleic acid (; DNA) is a polymer composed of two polynucleotide chains that coil around each other to form a double helix.

items.ask: What is the speed of light in a vacuum, in metres per second?

source.title: Speed of light
source.quote: The value 299,792,458 metres per second is approximately 1 billion kilometres per hour; 700 million miles per hour.

items.ask: In which country is Mount Kilimanjaro?

source.title: Mount Kilimanjaro
source.quote: Mount Kilimanjaro () is a large dormant stratovolcano in Tanzania.

items.ask: Which lake is the deepest in the world?

source.title: Lake Baikal
source.quote: Lake Baikal is a rift lake and the deepest lake in the world.

items.ask: In which year was Magna Carta sealed?

source.title: Magna Carta
source.quote: Magna Carta (Medieval Latin for "Great Charter"), sometimes spelled Magna Charta, is a royal charter of rights sealed by King John of England at Runnymede, near Windsor, on 15 June 1215.

items.ask: Which device is Alexander Graham Bell credited with patenting?

source.title: Alexander Graham Bell
source.quote: Alexander Graham Bell ( ; born Alexander Bell; March 3, 1847 – August 2, 1922) was a Scottish-born Canadian-American inventor, scientist, and engineer who is credited with patenting the first practical telephone.

items.ask: In which year did the Wright brothers make their first powered flight?

source.title: Wright brothers
source.quote: They made the first controlled, sustained flight of an engine-powered, heavier-than-air aircraft with the Wright Flyer on December 17, 1903, four miles (6 km) south of Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, at what is now known as Kill Devil Hills.

items.ask: Who invented the movable-type printing press in Europe?

source.title: Johannes Gutenberg
source.quote: Johannes Gensfleisch zur Laden zum Gutenberg (c. 1393–1406 – 1468) was a German inventor and craftsman who invented the movable-type printing press.

items.ask: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?

source.title: Sistine Chapel
source.quote: The chapel's fame lies mainly in the frescoes that decorate its interior, most particularly the Sistine Chapel ceiling and The Last Judgment, both by Michelangelo.

items.ask: Who deciphered Egyptian hieroglyphs using the Rosetta Stone?

source.title: Rosetta Stone
source.quote: Jean-François Champollion announced the transliteration of the Egyptian scripts in Paris in 1822; it took longer still before scholars were able to read Ancient Egyptian inscriptions and literature confidently.

items.ask: Which 1930 march did Mahatma Gandhi lead in protest at the salt tax?

source.title: Salt March
source.quote: The Salt March, also known as the Salt Satyagraha, Dandi March, and the Dandi Satyagraha, was an act of nonviolent civil disobedience in colonial India, led by Mahatma Gandhi.

items.ask: Which continent is the coldest?

source.title: Antarctica
source.quote: Antarctica is, on average, the coldest, driest, and windiest of the continents, and has the highest average elevation.

items.ask: Which city hosted the first modern Olympic Games in 1896?

source.title: 1896 Summer Olympics
source.quote: The 1896 Summer Olympics, officially known as the Games of the I Olympiad, and commonly known as Athens 1896 (Greek: Αθήνα 1896), were the first international Olympic Games held in modern history.

items.ask: How many squares are on a chessboard?

source.title: Chessboard
source.quote: It consists of 64 squares, 8 rows by 8 columns, on which the chess pieces are placed.

items.ask: Which ocean does the Panama Canal link to the Atlantic Ocean?

source.title: Panama Canal
source.quote: The Panama Canal (Spanish: Canal de Panamá) is an artificial 82-kilometer (51-mile) waterway in Panama that connects the Caribbean Sea in the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean.

items.ask: In which country was Vincent van Gogh born?

source.title: Vincent van Gogh
source.quote: Vincent Willem van Gogh was born on 30 March 1853 in Groot-Zundert, in the predominantly Catholic province of North Brabant in the Netherlands.

items.ask: In which country is Mount Fuji?

source.title: Mount Fuji
source.quote: Mount Fuji (富士山・富士の山, Fujisan, Fuji no Yama) is an active stratovolcano located on the Japanese island of Honshu, with a summit elevation of 3,776.24 m (12,389 ft 3 in).

items.ask: Which theorem relates the sides of a right-angled triangle?

source.title: Pythagorean theorem
source.quote: In mathematics, the Pythagorean theorem or Pythagoras's theorem is a fundamental relation in Euclidean geometry between the three sides of a right triangle.

items.ask: In which year was the Hubble Space Telescope launched?

source.title: Hubble Space Telescope
source.quote: The Hubble Space Telescope (HST or Hubble) is a space telescope that was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 and remains in operation.

items.ask: When did Albert Einstein win his second Nobel Prize?

source.title: Albert Einstein
source.quote: He received the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for "his services to theoretical physics, and especially for his discovery of the law of the photoelectric effect".

items.ask: In which year did Marie Curie win the Nobel Prize in Literature?

source.title: Marie Curie
source.quote: She won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry "[for] the discovery of the elements radium and polonium, by the isolation of radium and the study of the nature and compounds of this remarkable element".

items.ask: What is the name of Venus's largest moon?

source.title: Venus
source.quote: Venus has no natural satellites.

items.ask: What is the capital of South Africa?

source.quote: Pretoria is the administrative capital, while Cape Town, as the seat of Parliament, is the legislative capital, and Bloemfontein is regarded as the judicial capital.

items.ask: What is the official language of Switzerland?

source.title: Switzerland

items.ask: Who invented the light bulb?

source.title: Incandescent light bulb
source.quote: Historians Robert Friedel and Paul Israel list inventors of incandescent lamps prior to Joseph Swan and Thomas Edison of General Electric.

items.ask: How did Napoleon's famously short stature shape his career?

source.title: Napoleon
source.quote: In fact, at about 168 cm (5 ft 6 in), he was of average height.

items.ask: Who wrote 'The Little Prince'?

source.quote: Antoine Marie Jean-Baptiste Roger, vicomte de Saint-Exupéry (29 June 1900 – c. 31 July 1944), known simply as Antoine de Saint-Exupéry (UK: , US: ; French: [ɑ̃twan də sɛ̃t‿ɛɡzypeʁi] ), was a French writer, poet, journalist and aviator.

items.ask: Which Polish city was formerly known in German as Danzig?

items.ask: Which Czech composer wrote the cycle of symphonic poems 'Má vlast'?

source.quote: Bedřich Smetana (2 March 1824 – 12 May 1884) was a Czech composer who pioneered the development of a musical style that became closely identified with his people's aspirations to a cultural and political "revival".

items.ask: Which Danish philosopher wrote 'Fear and Trembling'?

source.title: Søren Kierkegaard
source.quote: Søren Aabye Kierkegaard ( SORR-ən KEER-kə-gard, US also -⁠gor; Danish: [ˈsɶːɐn ˈɔˀˌpyˀ ˈkʰiɐ̯kəˌkɒːˀ] ; 5 May 1813 – 11 November 1855) was a Danish philosopher, Christian theologian, poet, social critic, and religious author who is widely considered to be the first existentialist philosopher.

items.ask: Who founded the Republic of Turkey?

source.title: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
source.quote: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (c. 1881 – 10 November 1938) was a Turkish field marshal and statesman who was the founder of the Republic of Turkey and served as its first president from 1923 until his death in 1938.

items.ask: Who wrote 'One Hundred Years of Solitude'?

source.quote: Gabriel José García Márquez (Latin American Spanish: [ɡaˈβɾjel ɣaɾˈsi.a ˈmaɾ.kes] ; 6 March 1928 – 17 April 2014) was a Colombian writer and journalist, known affectionately as Gabo ([ˈɡaβo]) or Gabito ([ɡaˈβito]) throughout Latin America.

items.ask: Which Hungarian composer wrote the opera 'Bluebeard's Castle'?

source.quote: Béla Viktor János Bartók (; Hungarian: [ˈbɒrtoːk ˈbeːlɒ]; 25 March 1881 – 26 September 1945) was a Hungarian composer, pianist and ethnomusicologist.

items.ask: Which scientist, born Maria Skłodowska, discovered polonium and radium?

source.title: Marie Curie
source.quote: Maria Salomea Skłodowska Curie (née Skłodowska; 7 November 1867 – 4 July 1934), better known as Marie Curie, was a Polish and naturalised-French physicist and chemist.

items.ask: Which Catalan architect designed the Sagrada Família?

source.quote: Antoni Gaudí i Cornet ( gow-DEE, GOW-dee; Catalan: [ənˈtɔni‿ɣəwˈði]; 25 June 1852 – 10 June 1926) was a Catalan architect and designer, widely known as the greatest exponent of Catalan Modernisme.

items.ask: Which Polish composer is known for his piano nocturnes and études?

source.title: Frédéric Chopin
source.quote: Frédéric François Chopin (born Fryderyk Franciszek Chopin; 1 March 1810 – 17 October 1849) was a Polish composer and virtuoso pianist of the early Romantic period who wrote primarily for solo piano.
